subject: Aldera bakeoff: recap, decision criteria, and next tests
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Sloan <emma@alderahealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@alderahealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Aldera bakeoff: recap and proposed tests

Hi Emma / team,

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and a proposal for next steps so we stay aligned before the bakeoff.

Top pain points we heard:
- 95th-pct latency spikes during peak inference windows (user-facing search).
- Embedding cost at scale for nightly batch scoring.
- Data residency and audit traceability for customer PII-targeted models.

Stated goals (from our conversation):
1) 95th-pct gen latency < 350ms for typical 2k token prompts.
2) Reduce embedding unit cost by ~30% without accuracy regression.
3) Ship an audit trail + KMS-backed keys for model inputs/outputs.

Decision criteria (proposed weights):
- Latency / P95: 30%
- Cost / unit economics: 25%
- Security & compliance (SOC2, KMS): 20%
- Observability / debugging: 15%
- Ops integration & runbook: 10%

Open questions we captured (please correct/add):
- Exact production prompt/sequence-length distribution (you mentioned a small tail of 8k tokens).
- Requirements for staging data isolation and retention.
- Any blocked competitors/features we should prioritize in tests (you referenced GoliathAI).

Proposed next steps:
- Attached: "aldera-mvp-test-matrix.xlsx" (test cases, datasets, pass/fail thresholds) and a short vendor comparison PDF.
- Redwood to run two focused test windows: (A) sustained throughput with your production mix, (B) cold-start and long-sequence tail (8k tokens) latency.
- Schedule a 30-minute sync to finalize datasets and start date — we propose week of 2027-05-03.

Ask from you: please confirm the preferred start date for tests and share the procurement timeline (target PO / decision by date). Also, if there are any additional compliance artifacts you need beyond SOC2, let us know.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: aldera-mvp-test-matrix.xlsx, redwood-vs-competitor-quick-compare.pdf

Logan — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick items from our side.

- Procurement: we are targeting a PO window in early May and hope to make a decision by 2027-05-20.
- Security: please include SOC2 report and a short note on in-transit and at-rest encryption (KMS / HSM). We will also need an answer on whether Redwood can guarantee tenant isolation for a staging pool (no cross-tenant KV leakage).
- Long sequences: GoliathAI reported better throughput on our 8k token embedding jobs — please call out how your batching/quantization will handle 8k sequences.

I attached a brief doc with our bakeoff constraints (aldera-bakeoff-constraints.pdf).

We can do the week of May 3 for tests; preferred start date is Tue 2027-05-04. Camila / Logan — can you confirm availability and whether the proposed tests in your matrix map to our internal success criteria?

Emma Sloan
Director, Search & Relevance | Aldera Health
emma@alderahealth.com

Subject: Re: Aldera bakeoff: recap and proposed tests — test design and competitor notes

Emma / Logan — appreciate the note, and good to see Tue 2027-05-04 as a candidate. Quick answers and a proposed test plan refinement: 

On the 8k token tail and GoliathAI:
- Redwood handles long context by (a) dynamic batching with windowed KV cache eviction, and (b) optional quantized kernels for larger sequence runs. In practice we see up to ~10% higher throughput on batched long-sequence workloads compared to naive batching because we avoid re-encoding shared prefixes. The attached compare PDF highlights where Goliath trades off KV cache for lower memory usage (they can push throughput but sometimes at the cost of latency variance).

Proposed consolidated test cases (we shortened names to match your matrix):
1) Production-mix sustained run — 8 hours at your QPS with actual prompt mix (measure avg/P95/P99 latency, errors, token cost). PASS if P95 < 350ms and error rate < 0.1%.
2) Long-tail cold-start — 50 cold 8k-token requests dispersed over 2 hours (measure cold-start P95). PASS if cold-start P95 < 900ms.
3) Embedding batch economics — nightly batch at your 2M embedding units; measure cost delta vs current baseline. PASS if unit cost reduction >= 25%.
4) Security & audit validation — demonstrate KMS-backed key usage and 30-day audit log export. PASS if evidence and a reproducible export pipeline is provided.

Logistics / instrumentation:
- We will provision a dedicated ephemeral test pool in Redwood Dedicated (isolated) and provide temporary credentials + a read-only dataset snapshot. Marcus will provision the pool and coordinate load agents.
- We’ll push a lightweight observability dashboard to your Drive link and share real-time traces.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C4d-aldera-bakeoff (test artifacts), HubSpot:HS-45892 (deal).

Camila Reyes
